name: Thailand
headline_status: Cannabis is no longer a narcotic in Thailand, but since June 2025 flower can only be sold to people with a prescription, and a medical-only control bill is before Parliament.
summary: Thailand removed cannabis from its narcotics list in 2022, which led to thousands of dispensaries opening. On 26 June 2025 the Ministry of Public Health made buds a controlled herb and barred shops from selling without a paper prescription covering no more than 30 days. On 22 September 2026 the cabinet endorsed a Cannabis Control bill that would confine use to medicine and phase out existing dispensary licences by 2028.

possession_limit.value: No fixed public possession limit was found; prescription sales are capped at a supply for up to 30 days of personal use.

retail_sales.value: Licensed dispensaries (about 18,000 licensed in mid-2025) may sell flower only against a valid prescription and must source from certified farms; walk-in sales are banned.

medical_program.value: Prescriptions on the official paper form may be issued by doctors, Thai traditional and applied Thai traditional medicine practitioners, folk healers, Chinese medicine practitioners, pharmacists or dentists; each is single-use, unrefillable and capped at 30 days.

regulator.value: Ministry of Public Health, through the Department of Thai Traditional and Alternative Medicine (DTAM).

penalties.value: Shops that sell without a prescription face up to one year in jail and a THB 20,000 fine, and licences can be suspended.

purchase_age.value: Draft Cannabis Control Act would ban sales to anyone under 20 and to pregnant or nursing women.

tourists.value: There is no tourist exemption: visitors can only buy flower with a valid in-person prescription from a recognised Thai practitioner. Officials have reported a sharp rise in smuggling cases involving tourists.

timeline.event: Cannabis removed from Thailand's list of controlled narcotics
Health ministry notification makes buds a controlled herb and requires a prescription to buy
DTAM publishes draft Cannabis Control Act limiting use to healthcare
Cabinet endorses cannabis control bill and sends it to Parliament

pending.item: Cannabis Control bill: medical-only use, registration of plantations, three-year licences, and phase-out of current dispensary licences by 2028 unless shops become licensed medical facilities.
pending.status: Endorsed by cabinet 22 September 2026; awaiting Parliament.

faq.q: Is weed legal in Thailand in 2026?
faq.a: Cannabis is not a narcotic, but recreational sales are banned. Since June 2025 shops may only sell flower to customers with a valid prescription.

faq.q: Can tourists buy cannabis in Thailand?
faq.a: Only with a valid prescription from a recognised Thai practitioner, issued in person on the official form. Online or chat prescriptions are not considered compliant.

faq.q: Will Thailand make cannabis a narcotic again?
faq.a: The current plan is not relisting but a Cannabis Control Act that confines use to medicine. Cabinet endorsed the bill in September 2026 and it is now with Parliament.
